cards.explanation: The answer is God Himself. David says, “Earnestly I seek You; my soul thirsts for You.” He's standing in a dry land without water, and the thing he's thirsty for is God. Think about that, friends. I bet a lot of us would be dreaming about a cold glass of anything out there, and David's mind goes straight to God.

The answer is God's power and glory. David says, “So I have seen You in the sanctuary and beheld Your power and glory.” He's remembering a place he's been, and what he took in there was God's power and glory. Out in the dry land, he's still carrying that memory with him. I think a good memory like that is worth packing.

The answer is glorify. David says, “Because Your loving devotion is better than life, my lips will glorify You.” The loving devotion comes first, and the glorifying comes right out of it. His lips have a job and they're taking it seriously. Mine mostly say "one more minute" to my alarm clock.

The answer is False. He says, “So I will bless You as long as I live; in Your name I will lift my hands.” Nothing in the verse mentions leaving the wilderness. As long as he lives means as long as he lives, friends. No fine print on that one.

The answer is satisfied. David says, “My soul is satisfied as with the richest of foods…” He began thirsty in a dry land, and now he talks about the richest of foods. The psalm says his joyful lips will praise God. I think a man who sounds that full isn't leaving the table hungry.

The answer is True. David says, “When I remember You on my bed, I think of You through the watches of the night.” The night is long, and his thoughts stay with God. I think that beats my midnight brain, which delivers a to-do list nobody asked for.

The answer is in the shadow of God's wings. David says, “For You are my help; I will sing for joy in the shadow of Your wings.” God is his help, and that's the reason he gives for singing. He doesn't say he'll sing someday when things calm down, friends. He says he will sing for joy in that shadow.

The answer is that God's right hand holds David up. David says, “My soul clings to You; Your right hand upholds me.” Upholds means holds up. It's like a steady hand under a wobbly tray of cookies that was about to tip. David clings with his soul, and God's right hand upholds him.

The answer is True. David says, “But those who seek my life to destroy it will go into the depths of the earth.” That's a heavy line, friends, and it's okay to let it be heavy. The psalm turns here from David's praise to the ones who seek his life. It comes right after David says his soul clings to God.

The answer is king. The psalm closes with, “But the king will rejoice in God…” After all that thirst and all those heavy words, the last note is rejoicing in God. The psalm doesn't say more about which king, so I won't either. It ends on joy, and I like that for a closing line.

The answer is that the mouths of liars will be shut. David says, “all who swear by Him will exult, for the mouths of liars will be shut.” The reason is right there in the verse, friends. Those who swear by God exult because liars will be silenced. It's a quiet ending, and I think quiet fits.
